```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A multi-site laboratory or sensor panel, not neuroimaging.

```{r}
library(referent)
set.seed(4)
ref <- norm_simulate(300)
spec <- norm_spec(
  family = norm_gaussian(),
  location = ~ s(age, k = 6) + sex + s(site, bs = "re"),
  scale = ~ 1
)
fit <- norm_fit(spec, data = ref, outcomes = starts_with("marker_"))
print(fit)
scores <- predict(fit, newdata = ref[1:3, ], uncertainty = "conditional")
scores[, c(".row", ".outcome", "observed", "centile", "z")]
```

With many outcomes the wide view is often more convenient: `tidy()` gives
one row per marker with its fit status and effective degrees of freedom,
and `augment()` returns the target rows with a `.z_<marker>` column per
outcome, ready for [norm_joint()].

```{r}
tidy(fit)[, c("outcome", "status", "n", "edf")]
augment(fit, ref[1:3, ], uncertainty = "conditional")[, c("age", "sex", ".z_marker_01", ".z_marker_02", ".support")]
```
